main_point.en: God’s Word is our powerful weapon against Satan’s lies and against temptation.

christ_connection.en: Jesus stepped into our world and overcame the temptation Adam did not overcome. Jesus showed He is fully obedient to the Father. He is the only One worthy of undoing the consequences of Adam’s sin and bringing blessing to all people (Gen. 12:3). Jesus’s life of obedience led Him to the cross, where He conquered sin and death as our Savior.
christ_connection.zh-Hant: 耶穌進入我們的世界，勝過了亞當未能勝過的試探。耶穌顯明祂完全順服父神。唯有祂配得消除亞當犯罪所帶來的後果，並使萬民得福（創世記 12:3）。耶穌順服的一生引領祂走上十字架；在那裡，祂作為我們的救主，勝過了罪與死亡。

content.en:
1 And Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness 
2 for forty days, being tempted by the devil. And he ate nothing during those days. And when they were ended, he was hungry. 
3 The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command this stone to become bread.” 
4 And Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone.’”
content.zh-Hant:
1 耶穌被聖靈充滿，從約旦河回來，聖靈將他引到曠野，
2 四十天受魔鬼的試探。那些日子沒有吃甚麼；日子滿了，他就餓了。
3 魔鬼對他說：「你若是神的兒子，可以吩咐這塊石頭變成食物。」
4 耶穌回答說：「經上記著說：『人活著不是單靠食物，乃是靠神口裏所出的一切話。』」

title.en: Satan Flees When We Cling to Truth

content.en:
5 And the devil took him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time, 
6 and said to him, “To you I will give all this authority and their glory, for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whom I will. 
7 If you, then, will worship me, it will all be yours.” 
8 And Jesus answered him, “It is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.’” 
9 And he took him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here, 
10 for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you, to guard you,’ 
11 and ‘On their hands they will bear you up, lest you strike your foot against a stone.’” 
12 And Jesus answered him, “It is said, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’” 
13 And when the devil had ended every temptation, he departed from him until an opportune time. 
14 And Jesus returned in the power of the Spirit to Galilee, and a report about him went out through all the surrounding country.
content.zh-Hant:
5 魔鬼又領他上了高山，霎時間把天下的萬國都指給他看，
6 對他說：「這一切權柄、榮華，我都要給你，因為這原是交付我的，我願意給誰就給誰。
7 你若在我面前下拜，這都要歸你。」
8 耶穌說：「經上記著說：當拜主──你的神，單要事奉他。」
9 魔鬼又領他到耶路撒冷去，叫他站在殿頂上，對他說：「你若是神的兒子，可以從這裏跳下去；
10 因為經上記著說：主要為你吩咐他的使者保護你；
11 他們要用手托著你，免得你的腳碰在石頭上。」
12 耶穌對他說：「經上說：『不可試探主──你的神。』」
13 魔鬼用完了各樣的試探，就暫時離開耶穌。
14 耶穌滿有聖靈的能力，回到加利利；他的名聲就傳遍了四方。

content.en: Leaders: Pick up the sword (Eph. 6:17), and show students that they aren’t weaponless in their fight against temptation.
content.zh-Hant: 帶領者：拿起這把劍（以弗所書 6:17），向學生表明，他們在對抗試探時並非手無寸鐵。

content.en: “Jesus’s victory over the devil thus resulted not simply because of his knowledge and use of the Scriptures (as in Matthew) but also because he was ‘full of the Spirit.’ Thus unlike Israel, which failed in its wilderness experience, God’s Son was victorious. The Spirit’s importance in this is evident, and Jesus’s experience became a model of how Theophilus was to live out his life. Even as Jesus, ‘full of the Spirit,’ was victorious over the devil, so in Acts, Peter (4:8), Stephen (6:5,8; 7:55), Barnabas (11:24), and Paul (13:9) were also filled with the Spirit and followed in their Lord’s footsteps. Luke’s readers are exhorted by their example to be filled with the Spirit as well.”⁹
content.zh-Hant: 「因此，耶穌勝過魔鬼，不只是因為祂知道並使用聖經（如馬太福音所記），也是因為祂『被聖靈充滿』。因此，與在曠野經歷中失敗的以色列不同，神的兒子得勝了。聖靈在這件事上的重要性顯而易見，而耶穌的經歷成為提阿非羅應當如何活出自己一生的榜樣。正如耶穌『被聖靈充滿』而勝過魔鬼，照樣，在《使徒行傳》中，彼得（4:8）、司提反（6:5、8；7:55）、巴拿巴（11:24）和保羅（13:9）也都被聖靈充滿，跟隨主的腳蹤。路加的讀者也因著他們的榜樣受到勸勉，也要被聖靈充滿。」⁹

content.en: “The circumstances could not be worse for Jesus to deal with the offer of food in verse 3. Jesus’s circumstances could provide him a ready rationalization for giving in. The contrast of this temptation to that of Adam and Eve in the Garden of Eden could not be greater. Adam and Eve had everything they needed to eat, but Jesus meets Satan in the midst of hunger and deprivation.”¹⁰
content.zh-Hant: 「對耶穌來說，要面對第3節所提的食物誘惑，當時的處境不可能更糟。耶穌的處境很容易讓祂為屈服找到合理的藉口。這次試探與亞當和夏娃在伊甸園所面對的試探，形成了極其強烈的對比。亞當和夏娃擁有一切所需的食物，但耶穌卻在飢餓和匱乏中面對撒但。」¹⁰

title.en: Satan Flees When We Cling to Truth

content.en: “Jesus’s numerous quotes from Deuteronomy in response to these wilderness temptations recall another time and place where temptation and God’s chosen met in the wilderness. During the exodus, the Israelite nation failed this test. Jesus succeeds where Israel failed. What is more, the genealogy immediately preceding this account has named Jesus as Son of Adam and Son of God. The echo of Genesis 3 cannot be missed. What Adam failed to do as representative of all humanity, Jesus succeeds in doing.”¹¹
content.zh-Hant: 「耶穌在回應這些曠野試探時多次引用《申命記》，使人想起在另一個時間和地點，試探與神所揀選的子民在曠野相遇的情景。出埃及期間，以色列民族在這項考驗中失敗了。以色列失敗的地方，耶穌卻得勝了。此外，緊接在這段記載之前的家譜，已將耶穌稱為亞當的兒子和神的兒子。創世記第3章的呼應不容忽略。亞當作為全人類的代表未能做到的事，耶穌卻成功做到了。」¹¹

content.en: “The ultimate issue here is whether Jesus is the Son of God. That’s why Satan keeps coming at him this way. Satan’s real aim is to destroy Jesus’s sonship so that he might destroy our salvation, for if Jesus were to fall in any of these temptations, he could not be the sinless sacrifice that takes away the sins of the world. So Satan unleashes the most relentless demonic assault in the history of creation, and Jesus remains faithful to his Father through it all.”¹²
content.zh-Hant: 「這裡最終的問題在於，耶穌是否是神的兒子。這就是撒但不斷用這種方式攻擊祂的原因。撒但真正的目標是摧毀耶穌神兒子的身分，從而摧毀我們的救恩；因為如果耶穌在任何一項試探中跌倒，祂就不可能成為除去世人罪孽的無罪的祭物。因此，撒但發動了受造界歷史上最猛烈、最持續不斷的邪靈的攻擊，而耶穌始終在這一切中忠於祂的父。」¹²

content.en: The Greek word “devil” comes from the Hebrew word sātan. Sātan is a term for an accuser, slanderer, or adversary, rather than a proper name. We see many references to sātans in the Old Testament. But over time, the term became synonymous with Satan, described in the New Testament as “an enemy (Matt. 13:39); the evil one (Matt. 13:38); a tempter (Matt. 4:3; 1 Thess. 3:5); an adversary (1 Pet. 5:8); the father of lies (John 8:44); a murderer (John 8:44); a liar (John 8:44); a deceiver (Rev. 10:9); an accuser (Rev. 10:10); and one disguised as an angel of light (2 Cor. 11:14).”¹³ We know that Satan is limited; we can resist him and are urged to do so because he flees when we do (James 4:7). We often inflate the devil’s powers. God has given him limited power in the world—for now. His influence has earned him titles like, “god of this world” (2 Cor. 4:4) and “ruler of this world” (John 12:31). But never do we see that the devil can control or read believers’ minds, enter our bodies, or be everywhere at once. In no way is he like our Lord, Jesus Christ, who has dominion over all of heaven and earth, now and forever!
content.zh-Hant: 希臘文的「魔鬼」一詞源自希伯來文 *sātan*。*Sātan* 是指控者、誹謗者或敵對者的稱呼，而不是專有名詞。在舊約中，我們看到許多對 *sātans* 的提及。但隨著時間過去，這個詞逐漸與撒但成為同義詞；新約將撒但描述為「仇敵（馬太福音 13:39）；那惡者（馬太福音 13:38）；試探人的（馬太福音 4:3；帖撒羅尼迦前書 3:5）；敵對者（彼得前書 5:8）；說謊之人的父（約翰福音 8:44）；殺人的（約翰福音 8:44）；說謊的（約翰福音 8:44）；迷惑人的（啟示錄 10:9）；控告者（啟示錄 10:10）；以及裝作光明天使的（哥林多後書 11:14）。」¹³ 我們知道撒但的能力是有限的；我們可以抵擋他，而且聖經也勸勉我們如此行，因為當我們抵擋他時，他就逃跑（雅各書 4:7）。我們常常誇大魔鬼的能力。神目前只讓他在世上擁有有限的能力。他的影響力使他得了「這世界的神」（哥林多後書 4:4）和「這世界的王」（約翰福音 12:31）這類稱號。但我們從未看見魔鬼能控制或讀取信徒的心思、進入我們的身體，或同時無處不在。他完全不像我們的主耶穌基督；我們的主耶穌基督如今直到永遠，都掌管天地萬有！

content.en: Temptation is not the equivalent of sin. Instead, temptation can refer to natural and good desires that are twisted and directed toward pleasing self rather than giving glory to God. Jesus was tempted like we are (Matt. 4), yet He never sinned; He faithfully resisted temptation and followed the will of His Father. Knowing our weakness, we are to be on guard against temptation that may lead us to sin (Matt. 26:41), and we pray for God to deliver us from evil (Matt. 6:13).
content.zh-Hant: 試探並不等同於罪。相反地，試探可以是指本來自然且美好的慾望被扭曲，轉而以取悅自己為目標，而不是將榮耀歸給神。耶穌像我們一樣受過試探（馬太福音 4），然而祂從未犯罪；祂忠心抵擋試探，遵行父神的旨意。我們知道自己的軟弱，就應當防備可能引導我們犯罪的試探（馬太福音 26:41），並且禱告求神救我們脫離邪惡（馬太福音 6:13）。

content.en: Jesus, thank you for enduring temptation, not only to show us how to fight against it, but also to prove that you are the son of God—the perfect, sinless sacrifice. You did what none of us could do and stood against Satan’s lies. Help us to run to you for help when we face temptation and to believe in the truth of your word.
content.zh-Hant: 耶穌，感謝祢忍受試探，不只是為了向我們顯明如何抵擋試探，也是為了證明祢是神的兒子——那完美、無罪的祭物。祢成就了我們沒有一個人能做到的事，抵擋了撒但的謊言。當我們面對試探時，求祢幫助我們奔向祢尋求幫助，並相信祢話語的真理。

content.en: The longest amount of time someone survived without solid food is 382 days. Hospitalized under medical care, Angus Barbieri survived on tea, coffee, water, soda water and vitamins as part of his weight loss regiment. His first meal after 382 days was a boiled egg and buttered toast!¹⁴
content.zh-Hant: 有人在沒有固體食物的情況下存活的最長時間是382天。在醫療照護下住院期間，安格斯・巴比里以茶、咖啡、水、蘇打水和維他命作為減重計畫的一部分，靠這些度過了這段時間。他在382天後吃的第一餐竟然是**水煮蛋和奶油吐司！**¹⁴

instructions.en:
These optional activities are designed to help your students interact. You’ll find a Discussion Activity and a Cultural Connection, which touches on a relevant topic in today’s teen culture. Each group is different, so adapt these activities to fit your group’s needs. The goal is for

Ask the following questions, allowing time for students to share responses:

question.en: Is temptation a sin? Explain.
What does temptation feel like?
How can temptation lead to growth?

content.en: We’re all tempted by sinful desires, but temptation isn’t a sin. Our response to temptation can lead to sin. In the moment, we may feel like we have no choice but to give in, but if we’ll remember God’s Word, temptation can be an opportunity to grow stronger in our walk with God.
content.zh-Hant: 我們都會受到罪惡的慾望試探，但試探本身不是罪。我們對試探的回應可能導致犯罪。在當下，我們可能覺得自己別無選擇，只能屈服；但如果我們記得神的話語，試探就可以成為我們在與神同行的路上變得更剛強的機會。

cultural_connection.en: The world teaches us that sin isn’t a big deal; it’s normal to experiment; we’re only young once. Culture lowers the bar for sin, or eliminates it completely, and teaches that we all have our own truth. We try our best to keep these ideas from permeating our hearts and minds, but they creep in—especially if we stop paying attention, if we crack open the door to a sinful desire instead of closing it and walking away. We think we can handle just a little bit of sin and stop anytime. Sin doesn’t work on those terms; sin is slavery that leads to death (Rom. 6:16). And when you give it room, sin seeks to invade every part of you. You may sometimes feel like you have to sin because you don’t have a choice, but this is another lie from the enemy of your soul. You have the power of the Holy Spirit living within you, directing you to the way out. God won’t allow you to be tempted more than you can handle (1 Cor. 10:13), but you have to use the tools God has given you to stand: His Word and the help of His Spirit.

question.en: How did Jesus wind up in the wilderness? What does this show you about our lives?
question.zh-Hant: **耶穌如何來到曠野？這讓你看見我們的生命有何啟示？**

answer.en: After Jesus’s baptism, the Spirit, not Satan, led Him to the wilderness to be tempted. God led; Jesus obeyed. God allowed Satan to tempt Jesus to confirm His Sonship and to model how to overcome temptation. God allows us to be tempted, but He never does the tempting. Giving in to our sinful desires is what causes us to sin (James 1:13-15). God sometimes brings us to our own wilderness to face testing and trials to strengthen our faith (James 1:2-3). Jesus was no stranger to suffering, and we won’t be either, but we can trust that wherever the Spirit leads is for our good—to help us become more like Jesus, who endured temptation to give us grace and mercy in ours (Heb. 4:15).
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌受洗後，帶祂到曠野受試探的不是撒但，而是聖靈。神引導；耶穌順服。神容許撒但試探耶穌，以確認祂是神兒子的身分，並示範如何勝過試探。神容許我們受試探，但祂從不試探人。我們屈服於罪惡的慾望，就會犯罪（雅各書 1:13-15）。神有時會帶我們進入自己的曠野，面對試驗和試煉，堅固我們的信心（雅各書 1:2-3）。耶穌對受苦並不陌生，我們也不例外；但我們可以相信，無論聖靈帶領我們往哪裡，都是為了我們的益處——幫助我們更像耶穌；祂忍受試探，好在我們面對試探時賜給我們恩典和憐憫（希伯來書 4:15）。

question.en: Why do you think Satan tempted Jesus with bread first? Why would many people justify Him giving in?
question.zh-Hant: **你認為撒但為什麼先用餅來試探耶穌？為什麼許多人會認為祂屈服是合理的？**

answer.en: Jesus had fasted for forty days. Satan knew Jesus’s body demanded food. Physical hunger created an opportunity for Jesus to act apart from the Father instead of trusting His provision. We might wonder, “What was so wrong with Jesus providing food for Himself? Hadn’t He earned it?” The problem was that Satan began his temptation with “If you are the Son of God . . .” Jesus had no reason to prove Himself to Satan; Satan knew Him well. God had also confirmed Jesus’s identity at His baptism. Unlike the Israelites who failed to trust God’s provision in the wilderness, Jesus passed the test.
answer.zh-Hant: 耶穌已經禁食了四十天。撒但知道耶穌的身體需要食物。身體的飢餓使耶穌有機會不依靠父神而行，而不是信靠祂的供應。我們可能會問：「耶穌自己供應食物有什麼不對？祂不是已經有資格得到食物了嗎？」問題在於，撒但以「你若是神的兒子……」開始試探祂。**耶穌沒有理由向撒但證明自己；撒但很了解祂。**神也已經在耶穌受洗時確認了祂的身分。**與在曠野中不信靠神供應而失敗的以色列人不同，耶穌通過了考驗。**

question.en: What temptations do teenagers face today? Read Deuteronomy 8:3. How does seeing Jesus apply this verse show you the way to fight temptation?
question.zh-Hant: **今天的青少年面對哪些*試探*？閱讀申命記 8:3。從耶穌應用這節經文的方式來看，祂如何向你顯明抵擋試探的道路？**

answer.en: Many of us struggle with comparison, focusing our attention on what others have. Temptation strikes at our identity, leading us to question how God made us. Temptation pressures us to lower the bar for sexual purity; we’re lured to harmful websites and into toxic relationships. We are tempted to escape real life through substance abuse. We wrestle with finding our worth in worldly approval and popularity. Deuteronomy 8:3 says that God’s Word is more critical than physical food. In other words, we can’t survive spiritually without it. Here’s the reality: Jesus didn’t pull His “Son of God” card or use supernatural powers to defeat temptation; He battled Satan’s lies and temptations with the exact weapons we have: the Word and the Spirit! Jesus is the Son of God. But He wasn’t sinless because He tapped into some power we don’t have available to us. Jesus was human in every way, yet He defeated temptation because He chose to obey the Father’s Word. He showed us how to stand—by knowing and living according to God’s Word and by following the Holy Spirit’s voice. Though standing strong against temptation may seem way more difficult than this, it’s this simple: God’s Word sustains us. We can’t live without it.
answer.zh-Hant: 許多人都在與比較心理爭戰，把注意力集中在別人擁有的事物上。試探直接攻擊我們的身分，使我們開始懷疑神如何創造我們。試探迫使我們降低性純潔的標準；我們被引誘到有害的網站，也被引入有毒的關係中。我們受試探，想藉著濫用物質逃避現實生活。我們為在世俗的認可和受歡迎程度中尋找自己的價值而掙扎。申命記 8:3 說，神的話語比肉身的食物更重要。換句話說，沒有神的話語，我們在屬靈上就無法存活。事實是：**耶穌沒有打出「神的兒子」這張牌，也沒有使用超自然的能力來勝過試探；祂是用我們擁有的完全相同的武器與撒但的謊言和試探爭戰：話語與聖靈！**耶穌是神的兒子。但祂無罪，不是因為祂啟用了某種我們沒有的能力。耶穌在各方面都是人，但祂勝過了試探，因為祂選擇順服父神的話語。祂向我們顯明如何站立得穩——藉著認識並按神的話語生活，並跟隨聖靈的聲音。**儘管在試探中站立得穩可能看起來遠比這困難，但其實很簡單：神的話語托住我們。我們不能沒有它而活。**

title.en: Satan Flees When We Cling to Truth

question.en: Read Psalm 119:11. How did Jesus apply this verse? Can We really do the same?
question.zh-Hant: **閱讀詩篇 119:11。耶穌如何應用這節經文？我們真的能做同樣的事嗎？**

answer.en: Satan could never make Jesus sin; He could only suggest it. Didn’t the serpent convince Eve to sin by suggesting that she misunderstood God’s words: “Did God actually say . . .” (Gen. 3:1)? Isn’t this what Satan does with us too? He can’t make us sin; he can only suggest it. When we are tempted by our sinful desires and have a weak understanding of God’s Word, we allow the enemy’s suggestions to cause doubt and for doubt to become justification: “Well, maybe this isn’t really a sin? The Bible is outdated; culture has changed. Things have different meanings now. Surely, God didn’t really mean . . .” Adam and Eve allowed doubt to win, but Jesus showed us how to stand—on a firm foundation of the Word. He refuted every lie and every suggestion with truth; every word from Jesus’s mouth was the Word. God’s truth is like a light that exposes the enemy’s lies and shuts them down!
answer.zh-Hant: 撒但永遠不能*使*耶穌犯罪；他只能提出建議。蛇不是藉著暗示夏娃誤解神的話來說服她犯罪的嗎：「神豈是真說……」（創世記 3:1）？撒但對我們所做的，不也是這樣嗎？**他不能使我們犯罪；他只能提出建議。**當我們被自己的罪惡慾望試探，對神的話語又理解薄弱時，我們就容讓仇敵的建議使我們懷疑，並讓懷疑變成合理化的藉口：「嗯，也許這*真的*不算罪？聖經已經過時了；文化改變了。現在的事情有不同的意義。神肯定不是這個意思……」亞當和夏娃讓懷疑得勝，但耶穌向我們顯明如何站立——立在話語的穩固根基上。**祂用真理駁斥每一個謊言和每一個建議；從耶穌口中說出的每一句話都是神的話語。神的真理就像光，揭露仇敵的謊言並使它們止息！**

question.en: Is sin ever unavoidable? Look at 1 Corinthians 10:13. What does this verse show you?
question.zh-Hant: **罪有時是不可避免的嗎？查考哥林多前書 10:13。這節經文讓你看見什麼？**

answer.en: Satan tempted Jesus with “every temptation” (v. 13), and we can see three types in today’s text: needs, power, comfort. We often struggle in these same areas. We worry God won’t meet our needs, so we look some place else; we desire power and status, so we strive for popularity over holiness; we seek comfort over suffering and avoid the more difficult road of faith. We often put ourselves in situations where sin feels unavoidable, but we always have a choice to surrender our sinful desires and take the way out God promised to give us. We sin because we want to sin—because it’s enticing. But as we walk with Jesus, He changes our hearts to desire Him instead!
answer.zh-Hant: 撒但用「各樣的試探」（第13節）試探耶穌，我們可以在今天的經文中看見三種類型：需要、權力、安逸。我們常常也在這些相同的領域中掙扎。我們擔心神不會滿足我們的需要，於是轉向別處；我們渴望權力和地位，於是追求受歡迎過於追求聖潔；我們尋求安逸勝過受苦，避開信心中更艱難的道路。我們常常把自己置於罪看似不可避免的處境中，但我們總是可以選擇放下罪惡的慾望，走上神應許給我們的出路。**我們犯罪，是因為我們想犯罪——因為罪很誘人。但當我們與耶穌同行時，祂改變我們的心，使我們轉而渴望祂！**

question.en: Look at verse 10. What did Satan use against Jesus? Read 2 Timothy 4:2-4. What happens if we don’t know and rightly understand Scripture?
question.zh-Hant: **查看第10節。撒但用什麼對付耶穌？閱讀提摩太後書 4:2-4。如果我們不認識並正確理解聖經，會發生什麼事？**

answer.en: The situation is comical. Satan tried to use God’s Word against THE Word (John 1:1)! Jesus knew the Word and was full of the Spirit. Satan had no chance of bending truth. If we are going to stand against Satan’s strategy of bending truth to confuse us, then we can’t simply know the Word; we must have a right understanding of it—its context and how it applies. If not, Satan will weaponize truth by blending it with lies, convincing us to trust teachings that sound good but lead us astray.
answer.zh-Hant: 這個情況很滑稽。撒但試圖用神的話語對付「道」（約翰福音 1:1）！耶穌認識神的話語，而且被聖靈充滿。撒但根本沒有機會扭曲真理。**如果我們要抵擋撒但那套扭曲真理、使我們困惑的策略，就不能只*知道*神的話語；我們必須正確理解它——理解它的上下文和應用方式。**否則，撒但會把真理和謊言混在一起，利用真理作武器，說服我們相信那些聽起來很好、卻把我們引入歧途的教導。

question.en: Based on the passage, how much power does Satan have in tempting you? How can you defeat temptation that keeps defeating you?
question.zh-Hant: **根據這段經文，撒但在試探你時有多大的能力？你要如何勝過那不斷使你失敗的試探？**

answer.en: We often credit Satan for our sin. We say things like, “The devil made me do it.” Let’s get rid of that mentality because Satan has no power over God’s children. He can’t read your mind; he can’t be everywhere at once; he can’t force you to act on sinful desires. But he knows human nature because he has watched human history. The truth is that we have the power to walk away when we’re tempted. We can walk different paths and avoid the way of sinners (Ps. 1:1), but instead, we so often strive to walk alongside them— to get as close to sin as possible without touching it. Then we wonder why we keep falling into sinful patterns we’ve desperately tried to break on our own. We must look at where we’re walking and where we’re planted (Ps. 1:3). If we want to defeat temptation—if we’re tired of giving in and doing what we don’t want to do—then we must use the powerful weapons God gave us: His Word and His Spirit. We must actively engage with the Word— deeply and daily—and walk by His Spirit (Gal. 5:16-17).

content.en:
Jesus is fully God and fully man, which is a wonderful mystery about who He is and a powerful truth for us to hold tightly. Being fully man, Jesus understood what it means to be human and to face suffering, weakness, and temptation. Today’s passage tells us that Jesus was not just tempted in some of the ways that humans are tempted, but He was tempted in all the ways we’re tempted (v. 15). Because Jesus endured all suffering and faced every temptation, He doesn’t look at us with pity, feeling sorry for us. He understands what we walk through and has great compassion for us, identifying with us. To serve a God who understands suffering, grief, and temptation is to serve a God who is completely trustworthy.

Not only was Jesus tempted in every way, but He also faced every single temptation without ever giving in to temptation and sinning. This is where we see that He is fully God, perfect and without sin. While we are sinful apart from the blood of Jesus, the life of Jesus gives us great hope that no temptation is so great that we can’t resist and find victory. To be clear, we can never find victory over sin within ourselves and apart from God, but we can always find victory through the power of the Spirit and the truth of God’s Word. We are urged to go boldly to the throne of grace, meaning that we can confidently go to Jesus in our weaknesses. When we run to Jesus, we receive mercy for our failure and grace to help us in our need. Whatever you are facing today, go to Jesus with confidence—He loves you, He gets it, and He is ready to meet you with His grace and mercy.

question.en: What does it mean to you that Jesus sympathizes with your weaknesses and temptations? Why does it matter that we serve a God who gets it?
What sin or struggle are you facing and need to run boldly to Jesus to find his help, grace, and mercy?

prayer.en: God, thank you seeing me in my weakness and understanding my suffering. You’re perfectly trustworthy and give me great hope to keep running to you.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，感謝祢在我的軟弱中看見我，也明白我的痛苦。祢全然信實可靠，賜給我極大的盼望，使我能不斷奔向祢。**

content.en:
We find great encouragement and conviction in today’s passage. Verse 13 encourages us that no temptation we ever face is uncommon or impossible to resist, which means we are never alone in our struggle and never without hope of overcoming every temptation. The greatest encouragement from these verses is the reminder of God’s faithfulness. We will not find victory over temptation by our own willpower or strength but only by God at work in our lives. Because God has always been and will always be faithful, we can trust that He will always meet us with the power to endure suffering and overcome temptation.

The life of Jesus shows us a difference between facing temptation and giving in to temptation. He was tempted in every way, but He never once gave in. This gives us great hope but also shows that we can’t ever get away with the excuse that we couldn’t resist the sin. We can expect to face temptation and testing all the days of our lives because Jesus absolutely did. But temptation doesn’t equal sin. Sin happens when we choose to give in to temptation instead of running to God for the strength to resist. When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness for forty days, He fought against every lie from Satan and found victory against every temptation by clinging to God’s Word (Matt. 4:1-11). God’s Word is our weapon, a sword to protect us, help us endure, and equip us with what we need to fight well (Eph. 6:17). Fighting well is both running from something and running toward something else. Not only should we run far from sin, but we also need to run to God. We work to remove sin from our lives by the power of God, and we replace all ungodliness with His truth!

question.en: What temptations are you facing right now? Why is giving into temptation (and choosing sin) sometimes easier or more desirable?
How does God’s faithfulness give you hope that you can endure temptation and choose God instead?

prayer.en: God, it can be easy to believe the lie that resisting temptation is impossible, but I know with you, all things are possible. Help me run from all temptation and run to you for help and hope.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，相信「試探根本不可能抗拒」這個謊言很容易，但我知道，有祢同在，凡事都能。求祢幫助我逃離一切試探，奔向祢，尋求幫助與盼望。**

content.en:
Compromise is one of the main temptations we all face. Compromise is agreeing to meet in the middle for the benefit of everyone involved, but that’s not the kind of compromise we are talking about today. The temptation of compromise means to waver from godly living and settle for less than God’s best—to lower the bar when it comes to sin. When friends are living for the world and having a lot of (temporary) fun, you may wonder what it would be like to join them. You may feel tired of standing firm because settling would be so much easier. The temptation of compromise can sound a lot like: I’m tired of feeling left out. What’s the big deal? So what if I give in a little? I can get serious about living for God later or when I’m older.

Today’s passage provides guidance for finding victory over compromise. Paul encouraged followers of Jesus to walk carefully and wisely. From these verses, we see that wise people are those who are filled by the Spirit, who live from a place of constant gratitude to God, and who make the best use of their time. This requires courage and perseverance to walk the narrow way of Jesus, even when others choose to follow the crowd. When you find yourself wrestling with compromise from a place of loneliness, exhaustion, discouragement, or apathy, look to Jesus! Don’t get tired of doing the good work of living for God (Gal. 6:9). God will always equip you and strengthen you to endure whatever comes. Be filled by His Spirit and completely led by Him. Only then will you find a life truly worth living—the narrow way. And you’ll be a light for the world to see.

question.en: Where are you compromising? What is the root of that temptation (approval of others, exhaustion, discouragement, or something else)?
Write out a prayer confessing to God where you have compromised and ask him to help you live wisely.

prayer.en: God, when my heart is tempted by the things of the world, help me to remember that I only need you. Help me stand firm in your ways even when it feels like I have to stand alone because you are worthy of my heart.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，當我的心受到世上事物的試探，求祢幫助我記得，我所需要的只有祢。即使我感覺自己必須獨自站立，也求祢幫助我在祢的道路上站立得穩，因為祢配得我的心。**

content.en:
Our world loves to establish winners and losers. This competition can be healthy in sports, band, and other extracurricular activities, but it can be seriously dangerous when it leads us to live selfishly and self-righteously. Even social media sets us up to compete for followers and likes. When we are tempted to compete against someone else, we take our eyes off of Jesus and forget that He taught us to serve others in humility and love. Jesus calls us to set aside our pride and the desire to be “the best” in order to love people well. Seeking what’s best for ourselves and living with a mindset of “What’s in it for me?” can be tempting because the world justifies this way of thinking. Jesus calls us to a better way. In a world of competition and comparison, Jesus calls us to compassion and care.

Even Jesus, the Son of God, did not come to be served by others; His mission, even as the King of kings, was to serve others (Mark 10:45). Today’s passage commands us to do nothing out of selfish ambition (v. 3), meaning that we are to follow Jesus’s example of selfless humility and seek to serve others. While pride tempts us to think too highly of ourselves, shame tempts us to think too lowly of ourselves; neither of these are how God calls us to live. Considering others more important than yourself does not mean that your life has no value or that you are a doormat; instead, it is knowing that you are already fully loved and valued by God. This truth frees you to focus on caring for others, even at the cost of your pride, convenience, or time. It frees you from needing applause and attention because you’re loved deeply by God.

question.en: How have you felt the desire to compete with others? What are some of the ways you’re tempted to do things out of selfish ambition?
Read philippians 2:5-8 again. How will Jesus’s example of serving others change the way you live and serve others this week?

prayer.en: God, in a culture of competing and comparing, help me follow your example of selfless humility. Give me an unselfish concern for others, seeking ways to serve people, not looking for what’s in it for me.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，在一個充滿競爭和比較的文化中，求祢幫助我效法祢無私謙卑的榜樣。賜給我一顆無私、關心他人的心，尋找服事人的機會，不再只看自己能得到甚麼。**

content.en:
We are living in a world that says things like, “Live your truth,” “Follow your heart,” and “Do what makes you happy.” Similarly, throughout the Old Testament, God’s people repeatedly chose to disobey Him and do what seemed right in their own eyes. Time and time again, their choices led to destruction. If we know that sin is destructive, why do we still choose it at times? Because sin is fun and often feels good in the moment. In fact, Hebrews 11:25 describes it as a “fleeting pleasure.” Comfort tries to sell the lie that “if I feel like it, I can or must fulfill the desire.” Whether we are avoiding, escaping, numbing, or trying to find satisfaction in worldly comfort, this lie can lead us into watching shows or movies, listening to music, consuming harmful content, and making decisions that dishonor the Lord and destroy us.

Today’s passage reminds us that our hearts, or our thoughts and feelings, are sick and more deceitful than anything else (v. 9). Following your heart is dangerous because your heart, apart from God’s transforming work, is drawn to sin and darkness. By His grace and power, God transforms our hearts and changes our desires as we follow Him. But this requires discipline to turn from sinful desires, humility to let people hold you accountable, and perseverance to chase after the things of God. To be clear, the Lord cares deeply for you and wants the very best for your life, but the Lord’s very best for your life is more about your holiness than your happiness. God calls us out of comfort and recklessness and into courage and self-control.

question.en: Where are you tempted to choose what’s comfortable? Where do you need someone to hold you accountable?

What are some of the ways you are tempted to turn to temporary pleasures or fun found in sin? Write a prayer confessing where you are struggling and thank God for giving you a new heart and new desires.

prayer.en: God, when I am tempted to do what feels good, convict me, call me higher, and fill me with your truth. Help me desire you above all else and lean on you for the strength to pursue holiness.
prayer.zh-Hant: **神啊，當我受到試探想去做感覺良好的事，求祢使我知罪，呼召我追求更高，並以祢的真理充滿我。幫助我渴慕祢勝過一切，並倚靠祢賜我力量追求聖潔。**
